construction: How a figure is worked out: for one name on one day, take the put reading at the strike closest to 10 percent below that day's recorded stock price and the call reading at the strike closest to 10 percent above it. A strike only counts when it sits between 9 and 11 percent away from the price on its side, both readings must be for the same expiry, and a reading only counts as a put or a call reading when the record itself says which side it is. The figure is the put reading minus the call reading, in points: a positive figure means downside puts are priced richer than upside calls by that many points.
empty_note: In the recorded per-strike ledger, no name carries put-side and call-side readings at matched distances for the same day and the same expiry, so no figure is shown from that ledger for any name. That ledger holds strikes at and above each stock's price, with no side recorded for any strike, and no strike anywhere near 10 percent below the price. A figure from it will appear here only when it carries both sides.
